ideas.title: Counter-based append for append-only tables in loops
ideas.hypothesis: The real append win on LuaJIT 2.0 is a hoisted counter: measured 12.44x with the JIT on and 4.80x interpreted, the largest all-round win available and confirmed by two independent measurements. t[#t+1]=v recomputes #t, an O(log n) array-boundary search, on every append; a counter does not.
ideas.change: New ast_analyzer.py::_analyze_append_loop proving a local table is created immediately before the loop, only appended to inside it, and never passed somewhere that could resize it; new ast_transformer.py::_edit_append_loop inserting 'local n = 0' and rewriting to 'n = n + 1; t[n] = v'.
ideas.measure: tools/microbench.py (I-003) speedup >= 1.15x in both JIT modes, plus differential tests over tables with holes and early break, plus gates G4-G7 clean on a full corpus run.
ideas.notes: Enabled GAMMA corpus: 232 table.insert calls inside loops out of 682 total, and the same transform applies to the 701 sites ALAO already rewrites to t[#t+1]. Promoted above I-002 on the team lead's recommendation after the corrected benchmark. The aliasing proof is the whole idea and is where this can fail.

ideas.title: Confirm table_insert_append is worth keeping, then leave it alone
ideas.hypothesis: The first version of this beam ranked this second overall on a benchmark showing t[#t+1]=v at 0.77x under the JIT, and recommended demoting ALAO's most visible feature from GREEN. That measurement was an artifact of timing without GC control between runs and is RETRACTED. Corrected, and confirmed independently by the team lead, the transform is neutral under the JIT (1.00x) and 1.2-1.5x interpreted: a small real win, no regression, nothing to demote.
ideas.change: No transform change. Once I-013 can classify per-callback JIT mode, verify the 701 sites are not concentrated in JIT-compiled bodies where the fix buys nothing. Separately, correct reporter.py::PERFORMANCE_IMPACT and the README GREEN table, which rate this 'High' when the evidence says 'small, and only interpreted'.
ideas.measure: tools/microbench.py under the section-2 protocol (warm-up, collectgarbage per run, best of 9) reproducing 1.00x compiled and 1.2-1.5x interpreted; then the I-013 mode census over the 701 sites.
ideas.notes: Do NOT touch the transform before the mode classification exists. Enabled GAMMA: 682 call sites, 701 findings, still the largest GREEN pattern. Retained in the beam so the retraction stays on the record next to the original claim.

ideas.title: LuaJIT 2.0 microbenchmark harness (tools/microbench.py)
ideas.hypothesis: Nothing in the repo or the lab measures whether a rewrite is actually faster, and the first version of this beam proves how easily that goes wrong: it reported ALAO's highest-volume fix as a 23% regression on the strength of a benchmark with no GC control, and the conclusion survived until someone re-measured by hand. A harness with the protocol baked in prevents the next one.
ideas.change: New tools/microbench.py plus a bench/ folder of paired Lua snippets keyed by Finding.pattern_name, timed under lupa.luajit20 in both JIT-on and JIT-off mode, with warm-up, collectgarbage before every timed run and best-of-N all mandatory; wired into pytest as a slow-marked test so a pattern with no bench entry fails.
ideas.measure: Reproduces the corrected section-2 table within 10%; every GREEN pattern must clear gate G2.
ideas.notes: lupa 2.8 ships lupa.luajit20 = LuaJIT 2.0 on x64 Windows, the exact target VM. Note that jit.off(true,true) does not affect already-loaded chunks: JIT-off mode must use jit.off(f,true) on the chunk itself, or the harness silently measures JIT-on numbers twice. Enabler for I-001, I-005, I-009, I-012, I-039.

ideas.title: Compile-check rewritten files inside ALAO, not only in the lab
ideas.hypothesis: The corpus harness compile-checks ALAO's output externally and found zero failures across 513 rewritten files and 4743 edits, which is excellent - but the guard lives in the lab, so an ALAO user gets none of it.
ideas.change: ast_transformer.py::transform_file - behind a --verify-compile flag (default on when lupa imports), loadstring the new source under lupa.luajit20 and refuse the write on failure, recording the error.
ideas.measure: compile_failures_after_fix stays empty on a full corpus --fix, and a deliberately corrupted transform is caught by a unit test.
ideas.notes: The flag must degrade cleanly when lupa is absent, since lupa is not in requirements.txt. Baseline: 0 failures of 513 rewritten files.

ideas.title: pairs(t) -> ipairs(t) on provably array-like tables
ideas.hypothesis: pairs is the most common iteration construct in the corpus and ipairs measures 5.90x faster on a compiled trace. But it is 0.29x in the interpreter, the sharpest mode split measured, so the transform must be gated on I-013.
ideas.change: New analyzer pass accepting only tables built by a literal with contiguous integer keys or by append in the same scope, with no non-integer key assignment anywhere in scope; emit YELLOW, gated on the I-013 classification.
ideas.measure: Microbench in both modes, plus differential tests over tables with holes, string keys and embedded nil values.
ideas.notes: Enabled GAMMA: 2333 pairs() calls, 256 inside loops, 50 inside per-frame callback bodies. Changes iteration order and truncates at the first hole, so the array-like proof must be airtight.

ideas.title: table.remove(t) tail removal -> t[n]=nil
ideas.hypothesis: Removing from the tail with table.remove measures 13.44x slower under the JIT and 5.21x slower interpreted than assigning nil and decrementing a counter - the largest speedup in the whole measurement table.
ideas.change: New analyzer pattern for the one-argument table.remove form on a local table with a tracked length counter.
ideas.measure: Microbench both modes plus differential tests on empty tables.
ideas.notes: Downgraded: the enabled corpus contains exactly ONE one-argument table.remove call, out of 42 total. Fails corpus-relevance gate G1 decisively. Recorded because the measurement is worth keeping.

ideas.title: Stop swallowing parse and encoding failures
ideas.hypothesis: ASTAnalyzer.analyze_file returns an empty list for both unreadable (line 446) and unparseable (line 459) files, so a file that cannot be parsed is indistinguishable from a clean file.
ideas.change: ast_analyzer.py::analyze_file - return a structured failure or raise a typed AnalysisError instead of an empty finding list.
ideas.measure: A run over a corpus that includes known-broken files reports them as failures rather than as clean.
ideas.notes: Downgraded hard. The first draft ranked this top-8 on the strength of 4 parse failures found by parsing every file on disk; all four are in DISABLED mods and the enabled corpus has zero parse failures. The design hazard is real but the surfacing half is now covered by I-029.

ideas.title: Fix _apply_edits() containment, the confirmed dropped-edit bug
ideas.hypothesis: _apply_edits() resolves overlapping replacements by priority and drops the loser, but containment is not conflict. When a cacheable-global rewrite lands inside the argument list of a table.insert(...) that also has a table_insert_append edit, the inner edit wins and the outer append rewrite is discarded and never retried. Because --fix skips any file with an existing .alao-bak, the loss is permanent for a normal user.
ideas.change: ast_transformer.py::_apply_edits around line 2272 - apply a contained edit to the container's replacement text instead of cancelling the container; failing that, iterate edit generation to a fixpoint. Also return and report the dropped-edit count.
ideas.measure: Idempotence goes from 8 GAMMA plus 1 vanilla violation to 0, and the 8 leftover GREEN table_insert_append findings in the post-fix re-analysis disappear.
ideas.notes: Confirmed with a reproducer in reports/corpus-sanity-report.md section 4. Nine affected files; canonical case G.A.M.M.A. UI/gamedata/scripts/ui_inventory.script:807, plus five sites in vanilla luapanda.lua. Lost optimization, not broken output.

ideas.title: Scratch-vector reuse in loops
ideas.hypothesis: vector() allocation in a loop measures 10.47x slower than reusing one scratch vector in the interpreter, and 1.01x compiled - the flagship case for I-013's mode gating. ALAO already detects it as vector_alloc_in_loop (78 findings) but only reports it as RED.
ideas.change: Promote to a YELLOW transform: hoist 'local _v = vector()' before the loop and rewrite the body to _v:set(...). New _edit_vector_alloc_in_loop in ast_transformer.py.
ideas.measure: Microbench both modes plus differential tests; the escape analysis must be proven by fixtures where the vector is stored or returned.
ideas.notes: Enabled GAMMA: 1081 vector() constructions, 1007 of them vector():set(...), 52 inside loops, 27 inside per-frame bodies. Unsafe whenever the vector escapes the iteration.

ideas.title: Per-frame callback cost model
ideas.hypothesis: per_frame_callback does fire (88 findings), but PER_FRAME_CALLBACKS lists only 4 names and misses all 97 class update methods on binders and se_ classes, so it covers roughly a quarter of the 325 real per-frame bodies in the corpus.
ideas.change: Widen PER_FRAME_CALLBACKS to include actor_on_first_update and on_before_hud_update, teach the analyzer to treat a method named update on a class table as per-frame, then flag the expensive constructs in those bodies.
ideas.measure: per_frame_callback finding count rises from 88 toward a number consistent with the measured per-frame construct census.
ideas.notes: Measured inside the 325 per-frame bodies: 306 db.actor, 145 concats, 50 pairs, 27 vector(), 18 alife(), 15 game.translate_string, 11 level.object_by_id, 5 tostring, 3 ini_file r_* reads. Report-only, so risk is low.

ideas.title: Hoist #t out of a numeric for loop bound
ideas.hypothesis: A textbook hoist with 764 enabled-corpus hits and a measured speedup of 1.00x in BOTH modes, because LuaJIT already hoists the length out of the loop itself.
ideas.change: Would be a new analyzer pass plus transformer edit - but the measurement says do not build it.
ideas.measure: Already measured: 1.00x compiled and 1.00x interpreted. Fails gate G2.
ideas.notes: Kept in the beam deliberately as the worked example of an idea that hit count alone would have promoted straight to the top and that measurement kills. Expect pruned.

ideas.title: Retarget the math.pow(x,0.5) rewrite at math.sqrt
ideas.hypothesis: ALAO rewrites math.pow(x,0.5) to x^0.5, which is a small genuine improvement (1.05x interpreted, 1.00x compiled) and NOT the regression the first version of this beam claimed. But it leaves most of the win on the table: math.pow(x,0.5) to math.sqrt(x) measures 4.25x interpreted, and the residual x^0.5 to math.sqrt(x) step is still 4.12x.
ideas.change: ast_analyzer.py::_analyze_math_pow and ast_transformer.py::_edit_math_pow - emit math.sqrt(x) instead of x^0.5, and update the README GREEN table.
ideas.measure: Microbench both modes; corpus diff limited to the 25 math.pow sites.
ideas.notes: Enabled GAMMA: 25 math.pow call sites, so this fails corpus gate G1 on volume and is cheap enough to do anyway. The 'backwards' framing in the first draft came from comparing math.sqrt against x^0.5 without also measuring math.pow, which made a small win look like a large regression.

ideas.title: Trace-abort / NYI awareness for LuaJIT 2.0
ideas.hypothesis: The corrected benchmark shows the mode split is not about avoiding regressions, it is about picking the right transform. Everything ALAO ships is 1.00-1.03x on a compiled trace and 1.05-1.63x interpreted, while the transforms it does not ship split violently by mode: pairs to ipairs is 5.90x compiled and 0.29x interpreted, scratch-vector reuse is 1.01x compiled and 10.47x interpreted. A classifier saying which of the 325 per-frame bodies run interpreted is worth more than any single new pattern, because it decides which pattern to apply.
ideas.change: New LUAJIT20_NYI constant table beside the other tables at the top of ast_analyzer.py, plus _analyze_trace_aborts() emitting a per-function mode classification that _analyze_uncached_globals and _analyze_table_insert consult before choosing a severity.
ideas.measure: Classify all 325 per-frame bodies; cross-check a sample against jit.dumpon trace output run under lupa.luajit20.
ideas.notes: The NYI list must be verified against the bundled LuaJIT 2.0 build rather than recalled - that verification is part of the work. Gates I-002, I-005, I-009.

ideas.title: Replace the stale shipped report examples
ideas.hypothesis: The two *_report_example.html files in the repo root (22 MB and 4 MB) predate at least seven analyzer passes and show a distribution that no longer matches reality: 1172 table_insert_append against today's 701, and zero unnecessary_else against today's 621. They are the first thing a reader of the repo sees, and reading them is what led the first draft of this beam to wrongly conclude that eleven analyzer passes never fire.
ideas.change: Regenerate both from the current corpus runs, or replace them with a link to the lab run records and drop 26 MB from the repo.
ideas.measure: The shipped example's findings_by_pattern matches a fresh corpus run within noise, or the files are gone.
ideas.notes: Live counts now come from data/corpus/20260910-222240-gamma-analyze, so the regeneration input already exists.

ideas.title: Cache analysis results by file identity
ideas.hypothesis: Repeat runs re-parse everything, and a regression harness will want to run on every commit.
ideas.change: A .alao-cache.json keyed by path, mtime, size, alao version, cache_threshold and the experimental flag, storing findings, consulted in stalker_lua_lint.py::analyze_file_worker.
ideas.measure: Second full-corpus analyze run completes in a fraction of the first, with identical findings_by_pattern.
ideas.notes: Downgraded after the real timing: analyze is 13.5 s for 1503 files at 8 workers, so this saves seconds, not minutes. Invalidation must include every flag that changes analysis output.

ideas.title: Drop the per-file thread used for the timeout
ideas.hypothesis: analyze_file_with_timeout creates a ThreadPoolExecutor with one worker per file, so a full corpus run spins up 1503 executors to guard against a case that occurs zero times.
ideas.change: stalker_lua_lint.py::analyze_file_with_timeout - use one shared executor, or skip the wrapper for files under a size threshold.
ideas.measure: Analyze wall time on the full corpus, which must not regress and should improve.
ideas.notes: Zero timeouts across 1503 files at the current 10 s default.

ideas.title: Differential execution harness under a stubbed Anomaly API
ideas.hypothesis: Every ALAO transform is argued safe in a comment and never demonstrated. Differential execution of original versus rewritten chunks is the only way to make correctness a measurement rather than an argument.
ideas.change: New tests/differential/ loading original and rewritten chunks into two lupa.luajit20 states behind a stub module providing db, alife, level, vector, time_global and friends; drive each exported function over generated inputs and compare return values plus recorded stub calls.
ideas.measure: differential_failures stays empty for every GREEN pattern over the fixture set.
ideas.notes: Slightly less urgent than in the first draft: the corpus harness has now shown output compiles across 513 rewritten files, and the one real bug was caught by idempotence rather than by semantics.

ideas.title: Retune the default --timeout from 10 s
ideas.hypothesis: The default per-file timeout is 10 s, zero files hit it across the whole corpus, and the slowest single file parses in about a second. A 3 s default fails faster on pathological input without losing any real file.
ideas.change: stalker_lua_lint.py - change the --timeout default and document the measurement in the help text.
ideas.measure: Zero timeouts across a full-corpus run at the new default.
ideas.notes: Marginal. Depends on I-016 if the timeout mechanism itself changes shape.

ideas.title: Take the table.insert value span from the AST, not from text
ideas.hypothesis: _extract_table_insert_value at ast_transformer.py:229 re-parses the call text and splits on the first comma after the first paren with no string or paren awareness before that comma, even though the AST already carries the argument node.
ideas.change: ast_transformer.py::_edit_table_insert - use _get_node_span(call.args[1]) for the value span and delete the text-splitting helper.
ideas.measure: Fixtures with a comma inside the table expression; the corpus diff must be byte-identical since no corpus file triggers the bug today.
ideas.notes: Natural companion to I-008 since it is the same method family. No enabled-corpus file has a call in the first argument, so this is a fixture and fuzz bug rather than a field bug.

ideas.title: Add --force-refix for the test harness
ideas.hypothesis: Files with an existing .alao-bak are skipped on subsequent fix runs. That is correct for users and it hides idempotence bugs from any automated check, and combined with the I-008 dropped-edit bug it makes a lost optimization permanent.
ideas.change: stalker_lua_lint.py - add an explicit opt-in --force-refix flag used only by tests and the corpus runner.
ideas.measure: The idempotence gate can run without copying files by hand and reproduces the measured 8-violation baseline.
ideas.notes: Small enabler for I-008.

ideas.title: Widen EXPENSIVE_INDEXES beyond db.actor
ideas.hypothesis: EXPENSIVE_INDEXES has exactly one entry, db.actor. repeated_db_actor fires 78 times while db.actor alone appears 306 times inside per-frame callback bodies, and every other db.* property read goes untracked.
ideas.change: ast_analyzer.py - add db.storage, db.offline_objects, db.script_ids and db.actor_binder to EXPENSIVE_INDEXES; the repeated-call machinery already folds indexes into the same buckets as calls.
ideas.measure: Finding-count delta on a full corpus run with gates G4-G7 clean.
ideas.notes: Extending the constant table is the documented way to add engine knowledge, so this is low-risk by construction.

ideas.title: Cache loop-invariant level.object_by_id(id)
ideas.hypothesis: level.object_by_id is the most common expensive engine lookup in the corpus. The analyzer explicitly declines to cache it because different ids give different objects, but a call whose argument is loop-invariant is cacheable within that loop.
ideas.change: New analyzer pass restricted to calls whose argument is provably loop-invariant and whose result is not stored across frames; emit YELLOW.
ideas.measure: Differential tests covering object destruction mid-loop, plus microbench with a stubbed lookup cost.
ideas.notes: Enabled GAMMA: 496 level.object_by_id call sites, 209 inside loops, 11 inside per-frame bodies, plus 47 alife():object calls with the same shape.

ideas.title: Cache get_console() more aggressively
ideas.hypothesis: There are 141 get_console():execute sites in the enabled corpus against a caching threshold of 4 that catches few of them.
ideas.change: ast_analyzer.py::_analyze_repeated_calls_in_scope - measure the real cost of get_console() first, then consider a per-name threshold override.
ideas.measure: Microbench of get_console() against a cached local with a stubbed accessor; if it is a cheap pointer return this idea prunes.
ideas.notes: Worth measuring before building. The gap between call sites and findings may simply mean most scripts call it once.

ideas.title: Drop redundant tostring() in concat chains
ideas.hypothesis: There are 503 '.. tostring(' sites in the enabled corpus and the concat operator already coerces numbers, so the call is often pure overhead.
ideas.change: New analyzer pattern firing only when the operand is provably a number or string literal or a local with a known numeric assignment; emit YELLOW.
ideas.measure: Microbench of a tostring concat against a bare concat, plus differential tests covering a nil operand.
ideas.notes: Behaviour changes for nil: tostring(nil) yields the string 'nil' while concatenating nil raises. That alone probably keeps this report-only.

ideas.title: Encoding fixtures from the 27 non-UTF-8 corpus files
ideas.hypothesis: 18 CP1251 and 9 latin-1 files exist in the enabled corpus and nothing pins the encoding round-trip behaviour of --fix.
ideas.change: Copy a representative handful into tests/fixtures/encoding/ and assert that --fix preserves bytes outside the edited spans exactly, using the analyzer's detected _file_encoding on write.
ideas.measure: Byte-level comparison of fixture files before and after a fix that touches one line.
ideas.notes: detect_file_encoding() currently handles 100% of the corpus with zero failures, so this is regression protection rather than a bug hunt.

ideas.title: Wire up or delete whole_program_analyzer.py
ideas.hypothesis: 424 lines of cross-file symbol definition and usage tracking exist in the repo and are imported nowhere. Dead code inside the optimizer itself.
ideas.change: Either connect whole_program_analyzer.py behind a --whole-program flag for cross-file dead-code detection, or remove it.
ideas.measure: Cross-file unused-function count on the corpus, manually spot-checked against a handful of mods before anything is ever removed.
ideas.notes: unused_local_function already fires 71 times within files. Cross-file dead code in a mod ecosystem is dangerous to act on because other mods can call into a script by name, so report-only is the likely landing spot.

ideas.title: Raise the nil-fix and dead-code actionable rate
ideas.hypothesis: potential_nil_access is 1499 findings and unused_local_variable 1581, yet almost none are actionable: on a 207-file sample only 8 of 215 nil findings (3.7%) and 0 of 317 dead-code findings (0%) were fixable. Either the is_safe_to_fix and is_safe_to_remove gates are too strict or the detectors over-report.
ideas.change: Instrument ast_analyzer.py::_is_safe_nil_fix and the dead-code safety checks to record a rejection reason per finding, aggregate it, then relax the dominant reason.
ideas.measure: Actionable rate on the corpus, with differential tests proving each newly-admitted fix.
ideas.notes: Both rates are so low that the features are effectively inert, which makes this cheap upside if the gate is merely conservative.

ideas.title: Stop shipping AST nodes across the multiprocessing boundary
ideas.hypothesis: Finding.details carries node, scope, calls and globals_info holding live AST node references. Analyze workers pickle all of it back to the parent process, which may never need it since the transformer re-runs the analyzer in-process.
ideas.change: models.py and ast_analyzer.py - strip details to what reporter.py actually consumes before returning from a worker, keeping the rich details only on the in-process transform path.
ideas.measure: Analyze wall time and peak memory on the full corpus, with an identical report as the control.
ideas.notes: Downgraded alongside I-015: total analyze time is 13.5 s, so the ceiling is small. Needs a check that no reporter or HTML-highlight path depends on the stripped fields.

ideas.title: Put failure and edit data in the JSON report
ideas.hypothesis: reporter.py::_save_json writes only generated, summary and findings, so nothing a regression harness needs about failures is available. The corpus harness had to re-run ALAO's own analyze_file_worker over every file just to attribute failures, roughly doubling its runtime, and edits_dropped_overlap is null in every results.json because there is no source for it. That missing counter is exactly what would have exposed the I-008 bug on day one.
ideas.change: reporter.py - add parse_failures, timeouts and crashes arrays with full paths and error text, plus findings_by_pattern, findings_by_severity, and per-file edit and dropped-edit counts.
ideas.measure: The corpus harness drops its duplicate analyze pass and full-run wall time roughly halves; the reported counters match a manual count.
ideas.notes: Pairs with I-035 and I-037, which are the other two reporting gaps the harness had to work around.

ideas.title: Cache game.translate_string results
ideas.hypothesis: game.translate_string is a C call plus a string allocation and its result is immutable for the session, yet it appears 66 times inside loops and 15 times inside per-frame bodies.
ideas.change: New analyzer pattern suggesting a module-level memo table keyed by the string id; transform only when the key is a literal or a local that cannot grow unbounded.
ideas.measure: Microbench with a stubbed translate cost, plus a check that the memo cannot grow without bound on the corpus call sites.
ideas.notes: An unbounded memo is a memory leak in a game that runs for hours, so the key-boundedness proof matters more than the speedup.

ideas.title: Make global_write grouped or default-off
ideas.hypothesis: global_write is 5697 findings on the enabled corpus, 39% of everything ALAO reports, and it is RED so nothing is ever done with it. Anomaly mod style writes globals on purpose, so it is pure noise for anyone running ALAO to make the game faster.
ideas.change: ast_analyzer.py::_analyze_global_writes - emit one grouped finding per function with a count, the way uncached_globals_summary already does, and add a --no-global-writes switch plus a reporter.py::PERFORMANCE_IMPACT entry.
ideas.measure: Total finding count on the corpus drops sharply while the number of distinct affected functions is unchanged.
ideas.notes: Upgraded after the real corpus run showed the 39% share. Pure signal-to-noise work; no semantic risk since nothing is rewritten.

ideas.title: Context-gate math.pow(x,2) -> x*x  [RETRACTED]
ideas.hypothesis: RETRACTED. Filed because x*x measured 0.81x under the JIT and looked like a mode-dependent regression worth gating. Corrected under the section-2 protocol it is 1.00x compiled and 1.58x interpreted: a small win in one mode and harmless in the other, exactly what a GREEN fix should be.
ideas.change: Nothing to change. Kept in the list only so the retraction sits next to the original claim.
ideas.measure: Already measured: 1.00x compiled, 1.58x interpreted. No action.
ideas.notes: Expect pruned.

ideas.title: Corpus runner emitting the contract results.json
ideas.hypothesis: Every other idea's measure clause needs the same harness: extract enabled mods, analyze, fix, compile-check, run a second pass for idempotence, write the run record.
ideas.change: tools/corpus_extract.py, tools/corpus_run.py and tools/corpus_compare.py in the ALAO repo, writing data/corpus/<run_id>/manifest.json and results.json per the contract.
ideas.measure: Run records validate against the contract schema and reproduce the recorded baseline numbers.
ideas.notes: DELIVERED by the corpus agent. Extracts enabled mods only (1503 files, not the 2079 all-mods figure in CONTRACT.md), compile-checks every rewritten file under LuaJIT 2.0, and runs a full analyze + fix + idempotence cycle in about 90 s at 8 workers. Recorded as kept rather than dropped so the dependency stays visible.

ideas.title: string.sub(s,1,1) comparison -> string.byte comparison
ideas.hypothesis: A common micro-optimization folklore rewrite: compare a byte instead of allocating a one-character string.
ideas.change: Would be a new analyzer pattern over the 87 enabled-corpus string.sub sites.
ideas.measure: Already measured: 1.00x compiled and 1.10x interpreted, below the G2 threshold of 1.15x.
ideas.notes: LuaJIT interns short strings, so the allocation the folklore worries about does not happen. Expect pruned.

ideas.title: Separate the timeout counter from the parse-error counter
ideas.hypothesis: stalker_lua_lint.py:738 routes anything matching TimeoutError into the 'Files with parse errors' bucket. A file that exceeded --timeout and a file that will not parse are completely different problems, and the summary cannot tell you which you have.
ideas.change: stalker_lua_lint.py - split the two counters in the summary and in whatever the JSON report gains from I-029.
ideas.measure: A deliberately slow fixture increments the timeout counter and leaves the parse-error counter at zero.
ideas.notes: Zero of each on the current corpus, which is why nobody has noticed. Pairs with I-029.

ideas.title: alao_exclude.txt ships with VANILLA_SCRIPTS in it
ideas.hypothesis: alao_exclude.txt auto-loads whenever it sits next to stalker_lua_lint.py and it ships containing VANILLA_SCRIPTS, so anyone who names their vanilla corpus folder the obvious thing gets a silent zero-file run with no warning. The corpus harness had to override it with an empty list and add --use-repo-exclude to restore repo behaviour.
ideas.change: Ship the file empty or rename it to a sample, and print a loud line naming every excluded mod whenever the exclude list is non-empty.
ideas.measure: A run against a folder named VANILLA_SCRIPTS processes its files, and any non-empty exclusion is visible in the output.
ideas.notes: Cheap footgun removal. Found by the corpus agent when the vanilla corpus silently produced zero files.

ideas.title: Per-file failure detail is unusable at corpus scale
ideas.hypothesis: Per-file error lines require -v, which also triggers reporter.print_detailed() and dumps all 14,455 findings; and those lines print script_path.name rather than the path, so the many mods that all ship ui_inventory.script cannot be told apart.
ideas.change: stalker_lua_lint.py and reporter.py - print full paths in failure lines and decouple failure verbosity from finding verbosity.
ideas.measure: A corpus run can list every failing file by path without printing the finding dump.
ideas.notes: Third of the three reporting gaps the corpus harness had to work around, alongside I-029 and I-035.

ideas.title: --fix must not create new findings
ideas.hypothesis: Re-analysing the fixed GAMMA tree shows YELLOW rising from 3987 to 3989: two new string_concat_in_loop findings were manufactured by ALAO's own rewrites. Not a correctness problem today since YELLOW is never auto-fixed without --fix-yellow, but a transform that creates work for itself is a smell and may compound once --fix-yellow is in play.
ideas.change: Identify the two sites from data/corpus/20260910-222415-gamma-fix/, then guard the responsible _edit_* method in ast_transformer.py.

ideas.title: Promote string_concat_in_loop out of --experimental
ideas.hypothesis: This is the best-measuring transform in the whole table - 8.69x with the JIT on and 7.89x interpreted, the only one that wins big in both modes - it is already implemented, and it is locked behind a flag almost nobody passes. 205 corpus findings are sitting unclaimed.
ideas.change: stalker_lua_lint.py and ast_analyzer.py - move string_concat_in_loop from --experimental to --fix-yellow, or to GREEN if I-017's differential tests clear it. The existing safety conditions (variable initialized to empty string before the loop, simple 'var = var .. expr' shape) already encode the preconditions.
ideas.measure: tools/microbench.py in both modes, differential tests on the accumulator shape including early break and nested loops, and gates G4-G7 clean on a full corpus run with the flag promoted.
ideas.notes: Corpus: 205 GAMMA findings, 15 vanilla. It is the most structurally invasive rewrite ALAO has, which is presumably why it was gated, so I-017 should land alongside it. Cheapest large win available because the code already exists.
